Alt Text Description: Three-panel chart showing concept frequency distributions. Left panel: Zipf rank-frequency plot on log-log axes with exponent approximately 0.86 showing a power-law distribution of concept frequencies. Center panel: histogram of concepts per episode with mean 3.96, roughly normally distributed. Right panel: histogram of episodes per concept showing a strongly right-skewed long-tail distribution with 79 percent of concepts appearing in only one episode.

Square heatmap showing domain co-occurrence counts for eight knowledge domains. Color intensity indicates how many episodes span each pair of domains. Software Engineering shows the highest co-occurrence with all other domains. The Statistics-Mathematics pair shows a particularly strong focused affinity.

Two-panel chart showing vocabulary growth dynamics. Left panel: cumulative vocabulary curves on log-log axes for raw concepts (beta equals 0.931, nearly linear) and meta-concepts (beta equals 0.320, sublinear), following Heaps' law. Right panel: two null model distributions shown as histograms, a gray cluster-permutation null with mean beta 0.268 and a blue bipartite configuration null with mean beta 0.254, with the observed beta of 0.320 marked by a vertical dashed line lying entirely above both distributions.

Two-panel chart showing asymmetric concept flow between eight knowledge domains. Left panel: flow matrix heatmap where rows are source domains and columns are target domains, showing the fraction of target-domain episodes containing source-domain concepts. The matrix is visibly asymmetric. Right panel: scatter plot of broadcast reach versus porosity for each domain, with Software Engineering showing the highest broadcast reach and ML and Network Science showing the highest porosity.

Radial bipartite knowledge map visualization. An inner ring contains 499 meta-concept nodes colored by knowledge domain and sized by frequency. An outer ring contains 1908 episode nodes colored by their primary domain. Radial lines connect episodes to their constituent meta-concepts. The eight domain sectors are arranged around the circle. Cross-sector edges are visible especially emanating from the Software Engineering sector, illustrating directed concept flow from foundational to applied domains.

Diagram showing two specific episodes from different knowledge domains connected through shared concepts. Five shared meta-concepts spanning four domains are shown with solid circles and connecting lines between the episodes. Additional concepts unique to each episode are shown with dashed circles, illustrating how the bipartite structure captures cross-domain relationships that partition-based methods would miss.
